### Agent-runtime boundary method (when applicability is not `none`)

Keep these boundaries separate in the driver record and later C4 view:
- frontend/experience; backend/domain services; durable workflow/runtime; and model gateway;
- **MCP** for model/client access to tools and resources; **ACP** for an editor/client session with a coding agent; **A2A** only for independently deployed remote agents exchanging tasks and artifacts;
- a coding-agent host (for example, Claude Code or Codex) versus a product agent runtime. The former does not create the latter.

For every tool or remote agent, record caller subject, tenant, scopes, approval state, data touched, and audit correlation ID. Durable work also needs a resumable state, idempotency key, retry/cancellation policy, and a human approval resume point. Treat a framework or protocol as an option, not a default: its ADR records version/maturity, auth model, data residency, export path, lock-in, and replacement plan.

Method references checked 2026-09-19: [MCP authorization and tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server), [A2A task exchange](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/specification.md), [ACP editor-agent sessions](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol/blob/main/docs/protocol/v2/overview.mdx), [Eve durable-agent preview](https://vercel.com/blog/introducing-eve).

### Cognitive Principles (advisory)
When wireframing, apply `ux-psychology-pro` (invoke from src/skills/ or .agents/skills/):
- **Hick's Law** — primary screens cap at one dominant action per viewport
- **Miller's Law** — list/grid clusters cap at 7 items; group beyond that
- **Fitts's Law** — primary CTAs are large and close to the user's natural hand position (mobile thumb zone, desktop bottom-right or center)
- **Progressive Disclosure** — secondary actions hide behind expand/menu/overflow until requested

For desktop macOS surfaces, also invoke `macos-design` for window-chrome layout (top bar + sidebar + content) before drawing wireframes — desktop is a different design surface from mobile/web.

**Truthful copy (the truthfulness invariant, applied to the page — non-negotiable):**
- Every claim is true and substantiable. No invented metrics, no "10,000+ users" if it's 200, no fake logos, no testimonials you don't have.
- No fake scarcity or fake urgency. A countdown that resets, "only 3 left" that never moves, or a "launch price ending tonight" that runs forever is a lie — cut it.
- The demo video and product screenshots show the REAL product behavior with representative data — never staged mockups presented as live, never a feature that doesn't exist yet shown as if it ships today.
- Placeholder/representative numbers must be visibly representative, never dressed up as real results.
- Risk-reversal claims (guarantee, refund, trial) must match what the business will actually honor — confirm against Step 1.5, don't invent terms.
- A page that earns the click by lying earns the refund and the chargeback. Truthful copy is the marketing-amplitude expression of the same truthfulness invariant the app obeys.

**Ingestion contract — what makes a PRD `/goal`-ready:**
- `goal.stopping_condition` is the loop's exit check. It MUST be externally verifiable (a test name, a command exit code, a file diff) — never "the agent believes it is done." Loops exit on the external check, not the agent's say-so.
- `goal.proof_commands` are the commands the loop runs to prove the stopping condition. The agent pastes their real output as evidence.
- `goal.out_of_scope` are the loop's guardrails; they prevent the autonomous run from wandering into adjacent files (reinforced by Section 12 "Files NOT to Modify").
- `goal.max_turns` bounds the run. Large features use `slices[]` so each slice is its own bounded `/goal`.

### Human-gated compound learning (required)

The compound loop is powerful precisely because it persists. That is also its risk: an autonomous system that rewrites its own instructions, skills, or memory without review drifts silently. Apply the discipline:

- **No unsupervised self-modification.** Pattern files (`what-works.md` / `what-fails.md`), golden-case promotions, agent-authored instructions, and skill/eval updates are *proposed* by the loop and staged — never silently committed as live instruction. Promotion requires operator approval, or an explicit recorded delegation under the HITL contract; a review agent alone cannot supply that approval.
- **Stage, then promote.** The coordinator writes candidate learnings to `.sigma/memory/project/patterns/_pending/`. Promotion to the live pattern files (and any skill/eval re-run) happens only after the required approval. Git diff is the audit surface.
- **Evidence, not assertion.** A pattern is promoted only with the trace/commands that produced it — not because an agent summarized it as a win.

This keeps the loop compounding genuine, reviewed learning instead of compounding confident mistakes.

### Linear as live dispatch (when configured)

Wire the Linear project as the coordinator's work queue:

1. Record the repo → `linear.project` mapping in `runtime.manifest.json`
2. The coordinator agent:
   - Queries `linear.project` at session start for pending issues (labels `eng-task` / `exec-task`, state Todo)
   - Dispatches work to assigned agents through the detected host's supported task primitive; task packets carry the tracker issue identifier when one exists
   - Monitors issue state transitions (In Progress → In Review → Done)
   - Triggers Devil's Advocate + Gap Analyst as final gates (`needs-verification` label while gates run)
3. Worker agents:
   - Read and update the linked tracker issue through the detected host's supported integration; attach the PR and move it to review only after verification evidence exists
   - When GitHub Issues is the tracker, a PR may carry `Closes #<n>` so merge closes the issue
   - Without an available tracker integration, claim work through the TASKS.md contract and record the limitation
4. The queue replaces ad-hoc task assignment — every piece of work has a tracker issue (Linear when configured, else a wave-labeled GitHub Issue) or a TASKS.md entry. Never the retired SigmaHQ kanban — GitHub always owns the PR/branch/review/merge loop; when Linear is connected its issues two-way-sync once the operator enables per-repo issue sync in the GitHub<->Linear integration (PR-linkback only today)

- `.sigma/backlogs/implementation/TASKS.md` is the sole persistent queue (`/next-task` contract from Step 11.5); the coordinator uses the agent runtime's native task primitives for in-session delegation
